title: Global convergence of gradient-enhanced least squares Monte Carlo for high-dimensional American options
author: Jiefei Yang, Guanglian Li
work: Gradient-enhanced sparse Hermite polynomial expansions for pricing and hedging high-dimensional American options
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's advertised main theorem - the global error bound max_k \|u_k - \hat{u}_k\|^2 <= C (\Delta t + N \sum_k (E_k^best + E_k^stat)) of the gradient-enhanced least squares Monte Carlo scheme - and its own proof is the discrete Gronwall globalisation at source lines 698-708. The unit is not a qualification exercise because the counted claim cannot be reached without the whole source-local analysis that the unit retains: the linear-BSDE representation of the continuation value function, the gradient-enhanced least squares problem and its empirical risk, the Lipschitz assumption on the discounted payoff, the Malliavin integration-by-parts estimate of the backward Euler Z-component (Lemma 5.3) with its Ito-isometry and martingale-representation argument, the estimate of the continuous-least-squares error (Theorem 5.4) obtained from the optimality of the continuous minimiser, the tower property, Jensen's inequality and Young's inequality, the one-step propagation (Corollary 5.5) including the max-identity that turns the continuation value into the value function and the statistical error of the discrete regression, and the hyperbolic-cross best-approximation lemma (Lemma 5.2). Combining Malliavin calculus, BSDE one-step error propagation, weighted Sobolev Hermite approximation and Monte Carlo statistical error into one dimension-free global bound is research-level numerical analysis for mathematical finance, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
